tools.description:
Search arXiv preprints directly (freshest source for new preprints).

Free text becomes an all-fields AND query; arXiv field syntax passes
through unchanged (ti:, au:, abs:, cat:, e.g. `ti:lattice AND au:Peikert`).
`category` limits results to one arXiv category such as cs.CR or quant-ph.
Year filters use the submission date. `sort`: relevance or newest.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_arxiv_search

tools.description:
Search Crossref, the registry of DOIs for journals, proceedings, and books.

Useful for resolving a half-remembered citation to its DOI and publisher
record. Filters: publication year range and author.
`sort`: relevance, cited, or newest.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_crossref_search

tools.description:
Search DBLP, the curated computer-science bibliography, newest first.

Every keyword must appear in the title ("quoted phrases" stay together).
`author` is a case-insensitive substring of the DBLP author name.
`venue` accepts CRYPTO, EUROCRYPT, ASIACRYPT, CHES/TCHES, FSE/ToSC, JoC,
PKC, TCC, CT-RSA, PQCrypto, SAC, COSADE, CARDIS, DCC, CiC, ePrint, CCS, S&P,
USENIX Security, NDSS, EuroS&P, ACNS, ESORICS, CSF, TIFS, TDSC, CoRR, or a
DBLP stream key such as conf/crypto or journals/tches; other text
matches a substring of DBLP's venue label. At least one of keywords,
author, or venue is required. `peer_reviewed_only` drops arXiv/ePrint
preprint records. Queries take a few seconds.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_dblp_search

tools.description:
Search OpenAlex, an open index of ~250M works with abstracts and citations.

Filters: publication year range, author name, and open access only.
`sort`: relevance (default), cited (most cited first), or newest.
Results carry OpenAlex IDs (W...) for paper_details and paper_citations,
and link a legal open-access PDF when one is known.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_openalex_search

tools.description:
List papers that cite a paper, or the papers it references (OpenAlex).

To see who cites a paper, use the library's related_papers: it calls
this, adds the citing sentences of the papers it holds and says what is
held of each. This is the index alone, for a program or a caller
without the library.

`direction`: cited_by (later work citing it) or references (work it
cites). `identifier`: DOI, arXiv ID, OpenAlex work ID, or Semantic
Scholar ID. `limit`: up to 200 a page. `sort`: cited (most cited
first), newest, relevance, or cited_per_year (citations per year since
publication, among the 200 most cited: the recent work others build on
before old classics). `year_from`/`year_to` bound the listed papers'
publication years — with cited_by and cited_per_year or newest, the
current state of the art built on a landmark paper. `format="json"`
returns the records as plain data, with the OpenAlex id and the total.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_paper_citations

tools.description:
Every full-text copy one paper is known to have, in the order worth trying.

`identifier`: a DOI, an arXiv ID, an OpenAlex work ID (W...), a Semantic
Scholar paper ID, or CorpusId:<n>. One link per line: the arXiv copy, the
author and repository pages Semantic Scholar's crawl found, OpenAlex's
open-access locations, Google Scholar's PDF link, Unpaywall's best copy,
and the publisher's link last. Nothing is downloaded or verified here; a
link counts only once its first bytes have been read. For the paper's
metadata use paper_details; to find papers use search_papers.
`format="json"` returns the copies as plain data, for a program.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_paper_copies

tools.description:
Full metadata for one paper: abstract, authors, venue, citations, PDFs.

`identifier`: a DOI (10.xxxx/..., doi.org URL), an arXiv ID or URL, an
OpenAlex work ID (W...), a Semantic Scholar paper ID (40 hex characters
or URL), or CorpusId:<n>. Combines OpenAlex with Semantic Scholar (TL;DR,
influential citations) and falls back to Crossref or arXiv. `source`
(crossref, arxiv or openalex) asks that index alone for its own record —
Crossref's work type, arXiv's primary category — which a program may
need; `format="json"` returns the record as plain data.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_paper_details

tools.description: Report which sources are configured and per-source request counters.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_paper_search_health

tools.description:
Many papers' records at once, by DOI, arXiv ID or OpenAlex work ID: titles, every author,
year, venue and identifiers, for a program filling its own records. DOIs and OpenAlex IDs go to
OpenAlex 50 a request, DOIs to Crossref too (50 a request), arXiv IDs to arXiv 100 a request; up to
500 identifiers a call. Where Crossref registers the DOI its author list is given, with `families`
naming each author's family name (a given name it has as initials spelled out from OpenAlex's). The reply
(JSON by default) lists `found` as {identifier, paper} in the order given, then `missing` and
`notes`; `format="text"` prints one line a paper. For one paper's full record, with Semantic
Scholar's TL;DR, use paper_details.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_papers_by_ids

tools.description:
Search Google Scholar (via Serper) for papers, with citation counts.

Broadest coverage, including books, theses, and publisher pages that
other indexes miss. Results include a publication line (authors, venue,
year), a snippet, "cited by" counts, and a PDF link when Scholar shows
one. Supports Google Scholar operators in `query`, e.g.
author:"Last Name", intitle:word, or "exact phrase". Each page holds up
to ten results (`num` trims the page); `page` continues. Each call is
billed by Serper; repeated identical calls within an hour are cached.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_scholar_search

tools.description:
Search several scholarly sources at once and merge the results.

To find papers, use the library's find_papers: it calls this, adds the
papers the library holds, says what is held of each and registers them
for fetch_paper and read_paper. This is the indexes and the ePrint
archive alone, for a program or a caller without the library.

Queries the sources in parallel, each for its own `per_source` best
text matches, merges duplicates by DOI, arXiv ID, or title, and orders
the merged pool by `sort`: relevance (default: papers found by more
sources and ranked higher first), newest, cited (most cited first), or
cited_per_year (citations per year since publication, which lifts the
recent work others build on above the old classics; a survey still
rises with them).

Depth: `limit` results from `offset` on, up to 500 a call. per_source
defaults to offset + limit (at least 8 for relevance, 20 for the other
sorts) and goes up to 200 a source (Google Scholar 50, a paid credit a
page of ten, the next page asked only after a full one), so asking for
100 asks every source for 100. A wider pool takes longer: about a
minute at 200 a source; each source has 30 s (100 s past 50 a source)
and then answers with what it has. For 100 or more results use
format="brief", one line a paper; paper_details gives one in full.
Paging with offset is consistent when per_source is given.

Papers on topic come first: those whose title and abstract carry three
quarters of the query's terms, or that three sources found, or two
sources and half the terms. A hyphenated name is one term (ML-KEM,
SHA-1, SLH-DSA, A5/1, S-box; (EC)DSA is ECDSA), a name in capitals
stays however short (MQ, GF), and a standard's name and its scheme's
count as one (ML-KEM and Kyber, ML-DSA and Dilithium, SLH-DSA and
SPHINCS+, FN-DSA and Falcon, SIKE and SIDH); a query naming a scheme
or problem that way puts on topic only papers that name one of them.
Google Scholar's snippet is no abstract and is not counted. The other
sorts order those only; newest by the day of publication or posting,
a record dated by its year alone (OpenAlex's "2025-01-01") closing its
year. The pool is the sources' text matches whatever the sort, so a
paper that does not use the query's words is not in it; for the
current state of the art give `year_from` (the last few years) with
cited_per_year or newest, or ask paper_citations who cites a landmark
paper. Each merged record lists the sources that returned it.

Duplicates merge by DOI, arXiv ID or ePrint number, or by title with
the years and first authors agreeing and no identifier against it: two
papers of one title, or one paper's two DOIs (two volumes), stay two.

`sources`: any of google_scholar, openalex, semantic_scholar, crossref,
dblp, arxiv, eprint. Default: all of them (google_scholar only when
Serper is configured, eprint when the ePrint profile is). eprint is the
Cryptology ePrint Archive's own search, the whole archive with
abstracts, its records carrying the ePrint number (ids.eprint) and
posting date. DBLP matches every content word against titles, so it is
not asked for a query of four content words or more, and its matches
count by how much of the title the query is, not by its newest-first
order. Google Scholar's year filter applies to the results fetched.
Per-source failures are reported in Notes rather than failing the whole
call, and a source that fails after its first page keeps that page.
`format`: text (full records), brief (one line a paper), or json (the
records as plain data, for a program).
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_search_papers

tools.description:
Search Semantic Scholar (strong computer-science relevance ranking).

Filters: year range, venue (comma-separated names such as
"CRYPTO,EUROCRYPT"), and papers with an open-access PDF. Use
paper_details on a result for its TL;DR summary and reference counts.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_semantic_scholar_search

tools.description:
Search zbMATH Open, the mathematics index, in its own query syntax.

`query` is zbMATH's search string: `doi:10.1007/...` or `arxiv:2401.00001`
for one work's record, `au:Lusztig`, `ti:"flag manifold"`, `cc:14M15` for
an MSC class, `st:o` for works with an open copy, `py:2015-2020` for
years, joined by spaces (`cc:14M15 st:o py:2015-2026`). Each record
carries the work's MSC classes, its DOI and arXiv id when zbMATH links
them, and its zbMATH id; `page` counts from 0, up to 100 records a page.
zbMATH covers mathematics nearly completely, so no record for a DOI says
the work is not mathematics. `format="json"` returns the records as data.
tools.name: paper-search-mcp_zbmath_search
